title: Equal pay for equal work - the litigation trends in India
p1:
Can two employees doing the same job legally be paid differently in India? The answer is more nuanced than many assume.

Equal pay is not simply about comparing salaries. It is about whether differences in pay are based on valid factors or unfair discrimination.
p2:
A common misconception is that every salary difference automatically violates the law. Indian courts have repeatedly examined whether the work is truly equal in skill, responsibility, effort, and conditions before deciding such disputes.

One interesting trend is that courts have looked beyond job titles. Two people with different designations may still perform substantially similar roles, while the same designation may involve different responsibilities.
p3: The principle of equal pay for equal work comes from constitutional values and has influenced many employment-related cases in India. For businesses, transparent salary structures and clear role definitions can reduce disputes. For employees, documenting responsibilities and comparing actual work—not just titles—can make a stronger case.
